item: What the modification does vs standard ARMS logic
text_version: To achieve complete coverage of all base substitutions, a degenerate base “M” was used in the first position with the introduction of the specific mismatch base “W” at the third position to increase mutation specificity.
competing_version: the nucleotides at positions 1 and 3 from the 3′-end are identical to the nucleic acid sequence downstream of the fragment containing the targeted genetic variant
conflict: a perfect-match capture at pos -1 and a DELIBERATE mismatch at pos -3 are not the same as the usual ARMS rule (mismatch at the allele); the two extra bases behave as a 'downstream anchor', not as one mismatch
resolution: recorded, NOT resolved; nothing averaged or restated as a rule

item: Allele call vs template panel: 'only in the presence of the mutant'
text_version: These primer modifications confer high specificity to the mutated sequence, such that the amplification product is generated only in the presence of the mutant allele and not with wild-type genomic DNA.
competing_version: Table 2 reports 0/4 dipstick-positive among the four susceptible samples, so the WT arm was tested; this is consistent with the table, but see the mg_compromise note -- discrimination degrades at low DNA and 4 mM MgSO4, so 'only' overstates the generality.
conflict: the text's 'only' is a claim about the tested panel of 10, not a specificity bound
resolution: recorded, NOT resolved; nothing averaged or restated as a rule
